## Floating view rail and four approval modes

Nova Desktop 0.11.0 replaces the top view tabs with a floating icon rail on the right and adds an approval menu in the prompt composer. Approval and personality controls stay compact and use icons.

### Approval modes

- **Standard**: review tool permissions and plans requested by the harness.
- **Accept edits**: automatically approve recognized file-edit requests. Commands, unknown tools and mixed action batches still ask for approval.
- **Plan mode**: use Codex’s enforced read-only investigation sandbox. Desktop tools and other MCP servers are withheld. Choose a single Codex agent and stop running tasks before selecting this mode; unsupported harnesses show an explanation and are rejected by the backend.
- **Full access**: automatically approve ordinary tool and plan requests. Questions still require answers, and harness sandbox restrictions remain in force.

The selected policy also appears in Settings > Schedules. Existing manual/auto preferences migrate to Standard/Full access. Unknown saved values fall back to Standard, and the old auto-approval flag is removed when saving the migrated preferences.

### Interface improvements

- View navigation uses a floating vertical rail with tooltips, accessible names, Up/Down/Home/End keyboard navigation, and the existing shortcuts. Its reserved space keeps it clear of the editor and composer when resizing the window.
- The approval menu shows the current choice, an icon for each mode, and descriptions of its behavior. It supports keyboard navigation, Escape, outside dismissal and focus return.
- Personality keeps its icon or selected crew portrait, a consistent chevron and focus ring, a tooltip naming the current choice, and a visible native select in forced-colors mode.
- Running agents opens in a native popover with larger rows and an explanatory empty state. Selecting a running agent opens its chat, including when another view is active.
- The attachment button shows a pending state while choosing files and is unavailable without an open folder. Selected files remain editable paths in the prompt.

### Validation

- Frontend unit tests, lint, production build, Rust formatting, Clippy and Rust unit/integration suites.
- Windows/WebView2 app checks cover approval menu selection, edit auto-approval, question handling, Plan rejection for unsupported harnesses and running turns, agents focus and navigation, all 36 Desktop tools, five window sizes, five workspace views and nine Settings sections.
- Native file-picker selection and cancellation, dark/light visual inspection, 900×600 menu bounds and the forced-colors personality fallback.
- Packaged debug app checks exercise the embedded frontend and production CSP, including the Files editor regression.

### Limits

Plan mode currently requires Codex. Accept edits only approves adapter-recognized edit requests; an unknown request requires review. This release does not add per-member rows to Running agents or remove restrictions imposed by a harness.
